URI Board of Trustees – Finance and Facilities Committee Meeting September 14, 2026 4 Senior Vice President Benson provided an overview of the Total Budget request for FY28 as presented in the enclosure.
She noted that Associate Vice President John Poehlmann has led the effort for the development of the budget, as he has done in previous years.
This presentation focused primarily on the state appropriation portion of the University budget.
Senior Vice President Benson first compared the FY27 request ($156.7 million) to the FY27 enacted budget ($124.5 million), noting the breakdown of the request, including $5.0 million for Medical School planning.
Benson also discussed the all-funds FY27 revenue budget before moving on to a discussion of the FY28 budget submission, showing all projected sources and uses of funds.
Senior Vice President Benson then provided the assumptions regarding enrollment, tuition rates, and fees used in developing the FY28 budget, noting a small increase in undergraduate enrollment (<1%), a small decrease (1%) in graduate enrollment, and a 3% increase in tuition and fees.

Benson emphasized that these figures are for planning purposes only; the actual request for changes to tuition and fees will be brought to the Board in February.
She also discussed challenges to continued growth in undergraduate enrollment.
Senior Vice President Benson then discussed the FY28 State Appropriation request of $139.8 million (not including the medical school request of $7.0 million).
She noted that the University is planning for an $8.1 million budgeted operating shortfall.
The University is requesting a total of $146.8 million in state appropriations, including $7 million for the second year of medical school planning, which is presented separately from the University’s operating budget.
Benson also discussed the details within the Current Service Level request, including the largest portion related to Cost-of-Living Adjustments (COLA), a strategic increase in financial aid, a $5.0 million anticipated savings though position management, additional funds to aid URI Athletics operations, and additional funds to cover increased utilities costs.

Closing the presentation, Senior Vice President Benson discussed future year budget strategies, noting the University’s focus on enrollment strategies that emphasize new offerings and modalities, an increased focus on revenue generating opportunities, the ongoing careful management of staffing levels, and continued efforts to improve operational efficiency.
Senior Vice President Benson addressed Trustee Bovy’s inquiry about the state’s recent authorization increasing URI’s full time equivalent (FTE) employee cap.
Benson noted that, given ongoing financial pressures and personnel costs representing the University’s largest expense, URI is evaluating potential adjustments to the hiring process as it plans for FY2028.
The University intends to retain enhanced oversight of hiring to help control operating budget shortfalls.
President Parlange noted that the FTE restrictions apply to the unrestricted operating budget (Fund 100), with separate carve-outs for auxiliary operations, including housing and dining, as well as grant-funded research and sponsored programs.

Responding to trustee inquiry about the state’s funding of the proposed medical school at URI, Benson confirmed that there is legislative intent to provide an additional $7 million in FY 2028 and $8 million in FY 2029 to continue development of the state’s only public medical school.

Points to Consider: The University of Rhode Island launched its Workday implementation on January 12, 2026, to replace its PeopleSoft Human Resources and Finance systems and the PBCS budgeting platform.
The project has successfully completed the Planning stage and is currently in the Architect and Configure stage, where functional and technical teams are configuring business requirements, validating system design, and testing configurations to ensure alignment with institutional needs.
Overall, the implementation remains on track across the majority of workstreams and continues to perform within planned timeline and budget expectations.

Project leadership and governance have remained stable and effective, providing consistent oversight and decision-making throughout the implementation.
State system integration remains the most significant project risk.
Identified early in the implementation, this dependency continues to present challenges because critical aspects of the integration effort are outside the direct control of URI and rely on State of Rhode Island stakeholders and timelines.
URI and the State of Rhode Island leadership team have been meeting monthly on the project status.
Change management continues to be a key factor for the implementation.
Over the past several weeks, outreach and engagement efforts have increased to provide opportunities for faculty, staff, and campus stakeholders to learn about the Workday program.
These activities are focused on building awareness, preparing the University community for upcoming changes, and driving adoption to support a successful transition to the new system .
Overall, the project remains on track , however we are mindful and maintain focus on risk management, stakeholder engagement, and organizational readiness.

DISCUSSION ITEM a.
Review of Enacted State Budget Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance The Finance and Facilities Committee reviewed the FY27 state budget approved by the General Assembly on June 9, 2026.
Vice President Abby Benson reported that the General Assembly approved a $4.2 million increase to the operating budget, an amount in line with the Governor’s Recommended Budget (GRB), but well below the University’s request of $37.6 million.
She reminded the Committee of the three categories for the request: Operating Budget Shortfall, Current Service Level, and Strategic Initiatives, of which only the Current Service Level was funded.
She noted that of the $4.2 million increase in the operating budget, $1.3 million of this amount reflects support for corresponding expenses imposed by the state for centralized services.
Strategic Initiatives have not been funded for a number of years, but the University continues to maintain this request to signal the importance of these initiatives.

Vice President Benson also noted that the University received $15.2 million for general asset protection, $1.6 million for a campus access control pilot program (to determine the system of record for access control at RI), $8.0 million in RICAP ADA project support and also $18.0 million in RICAP Building Envelope work.
The Capital Improvement Plan included a GO Bond request for $165.7 million for the Integrated Health Building, with the legislature supporting the project at $165.0 million.
The bill also included Kushner authorization for URI to issue revenue bonds for Repaving and Hardscaping ($20.0 million) and Automotive and Administrative Services ($14.4 million).
The enacted budget included $5.0 million for medical school startup funds (operating).
Additionally, the full-time equivalent (FTE) cap was increased by 200 with a new auxiliary cap of 450 FTEs, inclusive of the total FTE count.
Committee members had no questions on the approved budget. 3.

Consideration of the FY2028 – FY2032 Capital Improvement Plan, and recommendation to the URI Board of Trustees.

Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance Vice President Benson provided a presentation on the FY2028 – FY2032 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).
She reminded the committee that the CIP is the first step in the budget submission process to the state, so this CIP is part of the FY28 budget submission.
The CIP is a rolling five-year plan submitted to the Board in April for its review and then in June for approval before being submitted to the state.
Vice President Benson noted that the presentation today focused on the changes to the CIP since the April review.
The plan includes $17.8 million for asset protection (RICAP), and two new projects on the Narragansett Bay campus totaling $16.8 million.
The Vice President discussed future projects, including a Marine Operations Building (necessary to receive the Narragansett Dawn) and Middleton renovation, both at the Narragansett Bay Campus.
She noted three projects that are being removed from the CIP: Ranger Hall Phase 2 (completed), Graduate

Vice President Benson also discussed certain proposed projects that are included in the Comprehensive Campus Plan, but not on the CIP, namely, a next phase of housing (with the delivery mechanism still under discussion), Plains Road parking structure (also with the delivery mechanism under discussion), decarbonization and geothermal projects, and a new natatorium complex.
She also reviewed the University's GO bond strategy, noting that URI plans to issue bonds in FY27 to support Service Sector projects, Utility Infrastructure, and Repaving & Hardscape Improvements.
In response to a committee member's question, she explained the different types of bonds and the role of Kushner authorizations.
Board Vice Chair Sabitoni added that the state's authorization for URI to use Kushner funds (revenue bonds) reflects confidence in the University's financial strength and its ability to repay the debt.

Vice President Benson noted in a final slide that the CIP is now presented to the state in an updated priority format, per their request.
She recognized Ryan Carrillo for his work on the CIP.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: October 26, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of FY26 Financial Statements Purpose of Submittal: This is a request to recommend to the full Board of Trustees the approval of the University of Rhode Island's audited Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) Financial Statements.
Points to Consider: URI’s external auditors, CliftonLarsonAllen LLP, have completed their audit and have no audit findings.
The University will have a clean audit opinion for the year ending June 30, 2026.
Upon approval by the URI Board of Trustees, the FY 2026 financial statements will be issued.
Please refer to pp. 4-14 of the enclosed draft financial statements for the University’s Management's Discussion and Analysis, which provides a summary of our FY2026 statements.
A few highlights are outlined below. • The University reported an increase in net position of $88.48 million in FY26, up from $65.90 million in FY25.

This includes a $8.18 million decrease in net position before $96.66 million in capital contributions, which significantly contributed to the overall increase. • In FY26, operating revenues increased by $15.92 million (2.96%), compared to a $4.62 million (0.85%) decrease in FY25.
This decrease in FY25 was primarily due to a change in NACUBO reporting guidance that increased the scholarship allowance, which nets against tuition and fees. • Net tuition and fee revenue increased by $16.33 million due to an increase in tuition rates of 3.5% for both in-state students and out -of-state students and an increase in demand for housing, along with stronger retention rates.
Other operating revenues decreased slightly as the University outsourced the bookstore operations. • In FY26, operating expenses for the University increased by $21.93 million (3.2%), compared to a $25.30 million (3.8%) increase FY25.

The increase is comprised primarily of increases in salary and benefits, as well as other operating expenses such as utilities, repairs, and maintenance which have been impacted by broader economic factors. • When reviewing the University’s condensed statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net position, it is important to note that nonoperating revenue plays an important role in supporting the operations of the University.
The primary component of nonoperating revenues is State appropriations.
The State’s unrestricted appropriation represents the largest component of the University’s nonoperating revenues.
The University of Rhode Island is an equal opportunity employer committed to community, equity, and diversity.

• In FY26, the University received $117.04 million in State appropriations for operations, up from $112.74 million in FY25. While the State general appropriation did increase by 3.18% in FY26, the final general appropriation represented only 17% of URI’s overall request. The State’s general appropriation plays a critical role in supporting the University’s operating expenses, so the University continues to advocate for support of its full general appropriations request.
